Second-pass review of Notre Dame's current Athletics Branding standards confirms the standardized 2015 interlocking ND monogram is the primary identifier across all sports. The Leprechaun is a spirit mark, shamrock is a secondary spirit mark, and vintage marks require special approval. Athletics assets are restricted to Athletics and must not be reconstructed or altered. Colors: Notre Dame Blue #0C2340, Standard Dome Gold #C99700; Irish Green #00843D is a spirit accent.

IU Athletics' official Brand and Uniform Guidelines use an identity ladder rather than one universal standalone mark. The IU trident is the core identifying mark and is also the official university logo; the guide distinguishes sport/marketing lockups from selectively used spirit marks such as Script Indiana and vintage marks. The current 2024–25 athlete book continues to feature the IU trident. Guide pages and current official material were reviewed, but no standalone production asset was captured and visually inspected; status remains partial. Official school colors are Cream and Crimson; the existing Crimson #990000 and White values are retained, with Cream treated as a core brand color in official applications. Do not elevate Script Indiana or a sport-specific lockup above the trident without an explicit application context.

Purdue's June 2025 official Brand Guidelines define the institutional logo as the Motion P paired with the signature wordmark; the Motion P is rooted in Purdue Athletics and has strong recognition, but should not be treated as a standalone official university logo. Public guidance does not establish a separate universal department-wide Athletics primary mark in the material reviewed. The official logo/brand guideline pages were reviewed, but no standalone Athletics production asset was captured and visually inspected; status remains partial. Official primary colors are Boilermaker Gold #CFB991 and Black #000000; the existing accent brown is retained as an accent only. Purdue Pete and the Boilermaker Special are separate spirit imagery.

Illinois Athletics' official logo page explicitly identifies the primary 'I' / Block I as the foundation and main identifying device for the Athletics brand. The Victory Badge / Athletics Shield is a secondary Athletics-only mark containing the primary Block I and must not be mistaken for the primary. The official page displays logo previews, but no standalone production asset was independently captured and visually inspected; status remains partial. The Athletics identity announcement confirms the Block I remains the primary representation and identifies Orange #E04E39 and Navy #13294B as the core palette, with white and grays secondary. Trademark use requires prior approval from the Licensing and Trademark Office.

Central Michigan Athletics' 2023–24 official Media Content Guide explicitly labels the Action C as the PRIMARY LOGO. The guide prescribes Gold/White on dark backgrounds, Maroon/Gold on light backgrounds, and a single-color brand-color version; the mark may not be stretched, rotated, skewed, recolored or given unauthorized strokes. The guide's page-5 artwork and examples were visually inspected, but they are embedded reference art rather than a standalone production file. No direct production asset was captured, so status remains partial. Official palette: Gold #F9AB18, Maroon #4C0027, White #FFFFFF and Gray #787878. The varsity Chippewa wordmark system is a separate team wordmark family.

Eastern Michigan Athletics' publicly available Style/Brand Guide (Version 2.0, August 2013) identifies the Athletics Block-E as its primary logo and distinguishes it from other university Block-E variants. A 2019 official Athletics history article independently describes the Block E as the primary athletic logo introduced in the department's rebrand. The guide is dated, and no newer public department-wide hierarchy or standalone current production asset was captured and visually inspected; status remains partial. The 2013 guide specifies Green #006633 and White #FFFFFF, with Black permitted. Marks may not be altered, distorted, rotated or combined with a wordmark; outside use requires written Athletics consent.

Western Michigan's June 2025 Visual Identity guide explicitly states that NCAA Division I Athletics uses the Bronco Spirit Mark as its PRIMARY logo and the institutional Brand Mark as its SECONDARY logo; the Spirit Mark is restricted to Athletics and is not for other university divisions. This supersedes the older 2016 Athletics announcement describing a block-W/Bronco-head combination as the primary logo. The 2025 guide displays the Spirit Mark with a WESTERN MICHIGAN wordmark as a composite reference lockup, not a standalone production file. No standalone production asset was captured, so status remains partial. Current primary colors are Gold #F1C500, Brown #532E1F and White #FFFFFF; gold is dominant. Contact marcom@wmich.edu to obtain approved creative assets. Do not substitute the institutional Brand Mark for the Athletics primary.

Toledo Athletics' official branding page explicitly states that the primary athletic logo is to be used for all Toledo logo needs and that the secondary Rocket logo is used only after the primary has appeared. The page provides separate PNG download links for approved primary background variants and prohibits stretching, distortion, rotation, discoloration or texture. The official page preview and branding-guide artwork were reviewed, but the primary PNG download targets were not captured as standalone inspectable production assets in this pass; status remains partial. Official colors: Midnight Blue #0B2240 (Pantone 289 C) and Athletic Gold #FFCD00 (Pantone 116 C). Sport-specific tags are sub-branding, and internal alternate identities must not replace the primary.

Ball State's official logo page identifies the Cardinal Head as the athletics logo for men's and women's intercollegiate athletics and reserves it for official Athletics business, including uniforms, publications, programs and licensed apparel. The 2025 university Brand Guidelines refer to it as the University Cardinal mark and distinguish the restricted retail-only vintage Dancing Charlie mark. Official guidance requires permission for all logo use; no standalone production asset was captured and visually inspected, so status remains partial. Official Cardinal Red is #BA0C2F and White #FFFFFF; Dark Gray #54585A is an additional neutral. Do not substitute the institutional Beneficence logo or vintage mascot art.

The University of Cincinnati's FAQ explicitly identifies the C-Paw as the primary brand for University of Cincinnati Athletics. The current Athletics & Spirit Marks page defines three Athletics marks—C-Paw, Cincinnati Wordmark and Bearcats Wordmark—and explicitly classifies the Bearcat cartoon as a secondary spirit asset, not an identifying mark. The public page displays mark sections/previews but no standalone production asset was captured and visually inspected; status remains partial. Official university primary palette is UC Red #E00122, UC Black #000000 and White #FFFFFF. Athletics marks are restricted to Athletics; use is subject to review and licensing approval.

Louisville Athletics' January 2023 official Brand Guidelines explicitly identify the Cardinal head ('The Birdhead') as the PRIMARY LOGO and default mark for most applications. The white trap/outline is required to separate it from dark or complex backgrounds, with limited cost-related exceptions. The updated Louisville wordmark is a supporting mark, while the Gothic L is supplemental and may be used in lieu of the primary mark only under its defined rules. The PDF contains reference artwork and diagrams; original vector files must be requested from Athletics, and no standalone production asset was captured and visually inspected. Status remains partial. The primary palette centers on Cardinal Red; the existing #AD0000 / black values are retained pending direct color-spec cross-check.

Kentucky Athletics' official identity guide identifies the interlocking UK as the PRIMARY IDENTITY and globally recognized primary symbol across all Athletics programs. The two-color UK mark is preferred; one-color is alternate. Kentucky Blue #0033A0 and White #FFFFFF are primary; Black #2C2A29, Cool Grey #C8C9C7 and Metallic Silver #A5ACAF are secondary/limited-use colors. The guide shows the mark and clear-space/color rules but does not provide a standalone current production asset; the guide explicitly prohibits constructing or scanning the mark. Status remains partial. Sport-specific wordmarks support, rather than replace, the primary UK symbol.

Ohio Athletics' 2026–27 official Branding Guide explicitly labels Arch Ohio as the PRIMARY LOGO, Attack Cat as the SECONDARY LOGO and Solo Attack Cat as the TERTIARY LOGO; Script Bobcats and Cursive Ohio are alternative logos. The guide shows hierarchy and approved color/background variants, but displayed marks are guide artwork rather than standalone production files; no standalone asset was captured and visually inspected, so status remains partial. The Athletics site now lists a newer September 2026 Brand Guide 9.5; its document content was not extractable during this pass, so the April 2026 hierarchy should be rechecked against that newer edition before production use. Official digital green is #154734, with Black #000000 and White #FFFFFF.

Miami University's official athletics/trademark style guide identifies the athletic M mark variations as PRIMARY MARKS and distinguishes the RedHawk mascot/wordmarks as separate marks. The current university-wide brand system now uses the Beveled-M with the Miami University wordmark for institutional communications; that university logo hierarchy must not be confused with the Athletics identity. The athletics guide is older and no current standalone Athletics production file was captured and visually inspected; status remains partial pending confirmation of the latest Athletics asset package. Official RedHawk Red is #C41230 and White #FFFFFF; Black is a supporting outline/neutral. Do not substitute the mascot character for the athletic M mark.

The current March 2026 BGSU Athletics Brand Standards continue to identify the Peek-A-Boo interlocking BG/falcon as the PRIMARY mark; the official Athletics standards page labels it 'Primary Peek-A-Boo' and provides JPG/EPS downloads. The official BGSU athletics-logo.png was captured and visually inspected in the earlier asset pass; the July 2026 'Marching Tradition Forward' campaign explicitly says the primary logo remains unchanged, while Marching Freddie is an alternative heritage look. Official FY26 palette: Orange #FD5000, Brown #4F2C1D, Tan #CDA077, Black #000000. Marks are controlled under CLC licensing; no distortion, recoloring, cropping or effects.

Akron Athletics' May 2022 official identity announcement supersedes the 2018 Z-logo guide: it identifies the modern stylized A as the new principal logo and anchor of a unified Athletics visual identity, with a companion Akron wordmark lockup. The Z is subtly incorporated as a heritage element; Zippy remains the mascot and is not the primary mark. The announcement displays launch artwork, but no standalone current production asset was captured and visually inspected; status remains partial. Existing Blue #041E42 and Gold #A89968 are retained pending direct confirmation against the current brand style guide. Do not use the superseded Z mark as current primary.

Kent State's current official Athletics materials show a family of marks, including the Kent State K, Golden Flashes/Flash imagery, and sport-specific Fearless Flash marks. The March 2026 Fearless Flash Store announcement describes a collection of licensed logos and team-specific sport marks, not a single department-wide primary. Public sources reviewed did not establish one universal primary Athletics logo or expose an official current logo standards document; hierarchy is therefore left conservative. No standalone production asset was captured and visually inspected; status remains partial. School colors are Navy Blue #003976 and Gold #EAAA00 with White as a supporting contrast color. Do not assume the mascot, student-section mark, or team-specific Fearless Flash is the department-wide primary.

WKU Athletics' official 2024 Feix Field release explicitly calls the WKU red towel the primary logo and confirms it remains at midfield; Big Red is the mascot/spirit character and appears separately at the 25-yard lines. The official field graphic and historical identity page were reviewed, but no standalone current production asset was captured and visually inspected; status remains partial. Official school colors are Red #C8102E and White #FFFFFF, with Black/Gray as supporting neutrals. Do not substitute Big Red for the primary red-towel logo.

UMass Athletics' official Style Guide identifies the three-color Power-U & Massachusetts marks as primary color options for dark and light backgrounds, with one-color versions as approved alternates. UMass Athletics formally adopted Power U as its department-wide primary mark in 2015–16; the 2023 university announcement explicitly says the new Collegiate M supplements rather than replaces the Athletics Power U. The PDF is a composite style-guide reference and no standalone production asset was captured and visually inspected; status remains partial. Official palette uses Maroon (Pantone Red 202 C), Grey (Pantone 32% Process Black C), Black and White; existing Maroon #881C1C retained pending direct HEX specification. Athletics marks are not appropriate for academic materials and require written trademark permission.

The primary mark is interlocking MT lettering with the flying horse/lightning graphic; secondary logo is separately limited. The official athletics logos page links the high-resolution Primary Logo PNG, which was opened and visually inspected. Verified direct standalone asset. Digital/non-apparel Blue #0066CC and White #FFFFFF are primary; Pewter #F0F0F0 and Black are secondary. Apparel and Nike uniform blues have separate specifications; do not interchange.
